subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose a plugin runtime caller for plugin-registered Gateway methods, and should that surface be raw method dispatch, an allowlisted request API, or typed service/capability contracts?
rationale: The API shape changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract or security policy.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, authorization rules, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep route-scoped dispatch only
options.body: Decline ordinary plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls and document the current authenticated HTTP-route dispatch helper as the supported boundary.

options.title: Expose raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Add a generic method-string caller and explicitly accept the larger security and compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, authorization rules, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the existing route-scoped dispatch contract and is the strongest history match for this Gateway/Plugin SDK boundary.
